Voltage Controlled Oscillator

Gallery:

See it in action

About the project:

This is a homemade voltage controlled oscilattor built on breadboards (i.e., a noise generator whose pitch can be controlled using signals of different voltages). I built this in my sophomore year of college by following online tutorials, namely tutorials by Moritz Klein.

I made a few changes to the design to fit the components available to me at the time, debugging issues using oscilloscopes and the speaker's output. Above, you can see a photo of the circuit for this project.

To briefly explain, the oscillator works by controlling the feedback voltage of a circuit featuring a capacitor and a 555 timer. This circuit creates sawtooth waves that can be controlled with a voltage generator. In the photos and video above, the voltage generator used is a keyboard with a CV out port.

If you click on the "See it in action" button, you can watch a video and hear how the oscillator sounds!
